title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache and matrix parallelism
author: Priya Kaur
description: Context: our monolithic GitHub Actions workflows for lint/test/release have grown slow and brittle. They run too many jobs in a single matrix, cause cache key churn, and make iterating on CI changes risky. This PR splits the workflows into separate, opinionated pipelines (lint, test, release) and introduces several hygiene and performance improvements: - split workflows so lint runs fast and in parallel with tests; tests are split by package group to reduce per-job runtime; release is isolated to the release pipeline with stricter gating; - reduce matrix size by grouping compatible envs and moving cross-matrix concerns to a single verification job; - improve cache keys and layer caching to increase hit rate across branches and forks; - bump GitHub Actions runner images and consolidate action versions (node-20, actions/checkout@v4, setup-node v4) to reduce future churn; - add lightweight build-only path for docs and examples to avoid running heavy integration on doc fixes; - add concise README and a migration note for contributors. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows (lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml) - [x] Implement optimized cache keys and restore logic - [x] Reduce matrix cardinality and group packages - [x] Update GH Actions versions and runner images - [x] Validate pipeline end-to-end on feature branch - [x] Update CONTRIBUTING.md and dev docs Related: ENG-2981 (CI hygiene), ENG-3120 (release automation reliability). Motivation: faster feedback loops for engineers, lower CI minutes cost, reduced flakiness during release automation. Notes: initial iteration caused a transient unit test failure in macOS-latest matrix due to an env mismatch; fixed by normalizing NODE_ENV and lockfile behavior. This PR does not change runtime code or customer-facing behavior.
